title: Katakana Voiced T-Row — ダ ヂ ヅ デ ド

points.name: ダ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as だ — 'da'; voiced version of タ
points.explanation: ダ makes the same 'da' sound as hiragana だ — voiced 'd' before 'ah', like in 'dark'. It's タ plus the dakuten. ダ appears in ダンス (dance), ダイヤモンド (diamond), and ダイエット (diet — in Japan, ダイエット specifically means weight-loss dieting, not the general English sense). ダイエット is interesting culturally: it's become one of Japan's most used health-and-beauty buzzwords, and you'll see it on food labels, TV shows, and magazine covers constantly.
rules: ダ = タ + dakuten; voiced 'd' before 'ah'.
ダイエット (diet) in Japan specifically means a weight-loss regimen — not just regular eating.
ダンス (dance) is widely used in pop culture, K-pop, and entertainment contexts.
points.flashcardAnswer: da — voiced version of タ; like 'da' in 'dark'

points.name: ヂ
points.shortDescription: Pronounced 'ji' — same as ジ in modern Japanese
points.explanation: ヂ is the katakana equivalent of hiragana ぢ — the voiced version of チ. Like its hiragana counterpart, ヂ is pronounced 'ji' in modern Japanese, identical to ジ. ヂ is extremely rare and you will almost never encounter it in everyday katakana writing. It occasionally appears in certain brand names, retro styling, or specialized typography. The key point is simply: if you ever see ヂ, read it as 'ji'.
rules: ヂ = チ + dakuten; pronounced 'ji' in modern Japanese — same as ジ.
ヂ is extremely rare in modern katakana writing.
When you see ヂ, simply read it as 'ji'. No special treatment needed.

points.flashcardAnswer: ji — same as ジ in modern Japanese (voiced version of チ; rare character)

points.name: ヅ
points.shortDescription: Pronounced 'zu' — same as ズ in modern Japanese
points.explanation: ヅ is the katakana equivalent of hiragana づ — the voiced version of ツ. Like ヂ, it is pronounced 'zu' in modern Japanese, identical to ズ. ヅ is also extremely rare in modern katakana and you will almost never see it. It's worth knowing exists, but don't worry about when to use it. An interesting historical note: ヅ and ツ are related by a phenomenon called 'sequential voicing' (rendaku) in Japanese compound words, but this primarily affects hiragana writing, not katakana loanwords.
rules: ヅ = ツ + dakuten; pronounced 'zu' in modern Japanese — same as ズ.
ヅ is extremely rare in modern katakana writing.
When you see ヅ, simply read it as 'zu'.

examples.english: (as in Takarazuka — タカラヅカ theater company)

points.flashcardAnswer: zu — same as ズ in modern Japanese (voiced version of ツ; rare character)

points.name: デ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as で — 'de'; voiced version of テ
points.explanation: デ makes the same 'de' sound as hiragana で — voiced 'd' before 'eh', like 'de' in 'desk'. It's テ plus the dakuten. デ is a very productive character in katakana loanwords: デザイン (design), デパート (department store), デジタル (digital), and デート (date — as in a romantic date). デパート is a distinctly Japanese cultural institution — multi-floor department stores in Japan are elaborate shopping experiences with food halls in the basement (デパ地下[ちか], depa-chika) that are legendary for their quality.
rules: デ = テ + dakuten; voiced 'd' before 'eh'.
デザイン (design) and デジタル (digital) are essential in modern business and tech contexts.
デパート (department store) + デパ地下[ちか] (basement food hall) — a uniquely Japanese retail experience.
points.flashcardAnswer: de — voiced version of テ; like 'de' in 'desk'

points.name: ド
points.shortDescription: Same sound as ど — 'do'; voiced version of ト
points.explanation: ド makes the same 'do' sound as hiragana ど — voiced 'd' before 'oh', like the English word 'door'. It's ト plus the dakuten. ド is one of the most productive katakana characters for loanwords: ドア (door), ドライブ (drive), ドラマ (drama / TV show), ドイツ (Germany — from 'Deutsch'), and ドキドキ (heart-pounding feeling, an onomatopoeia). ドキドキ is a wonderful expressive word: it's the sound your heart makes when you're excited or nervous, and is extremely common in anime, manga, and everyday speech.
rules: ド = ト + dakuten; voiced 'd' before 'oh'.
ドア (door), ドライブ (drive), and ドラマ (drama) are among the most common ド words.
ドキドキ (heart pounding with excitement/nervousness) — one of the most expressive onomatopoeia words.
points.flashcardAnswer: do — voiced version of ト; like 'do' in 'door'

chapterPractice.prompt: ヂ and ヅ are rare characters. What sound do they make in modern Japanese?
choices: ji and zu (same as ジ and ズ)
chapterPractice.explanation: In modern Japanese, ヂ is pronounced 'ji' (same as ジ) and ヅ is pronounced 'zu' (same as ズ). These characters are rare and mostly historical. When you see them, just read them the same as ジ and ズ.

chapterPractice.prompt: Which hiragana matches the katakana ド?
chapterPractice.explanation: ド and ど both make the 'do' sound (like 'door'). Katakana ド is ト (to) with a dakuten added. It's one of the most useful voiced katakana characters — appearing in ドア (door), ドラマ (drama), and ドライブ (drive).

chapterPractice.prompt: What does this katakana word mean?
chapterPractice.explanation: デザイン (dezain) means 'design'. デ (de) + ザ (za) + イ (i) + ン (n) = dezain. This is essential vocabulary in creative fields, advertising, and everyday Japanese conversation about aesthetics.

chapterPractice.prompt: What does this katakana word mean?
chapterPractice.explanation: ドラマ (dorama) means 'TV drama series' — the primary usage in modern Japan. ド (do) + ラ (ra) + マ (ma) = dorama. Japanese ドラマ are hugely popular both domestically and internationally.
